tools.name: ragify
tools.description: Ingest documents or text into LightRAG for RAG indexing. Supports file upload or direct text insertion. Returns a track_id for monitoring processing status.

file_paths.description: List of file paths to upload and index. Supports: pdf, doc, docx, txt, md, html, csv, json, xml, py, js, etc.

text.description: Direct text content to insert into the knowledge base (alternative to file_paths).

file_source.description: Optional source identifier for the inserted text.

workspace.description: Optional LightRAG workspace (tenant) name for data isolation. Use the same workspace consistently per category (e.g. 'customer_service', 'product_details'). Omit to use the server's default workspace.

tools.name: rag_query
tools.description: Query LightRAG knowledge base using RAG. Retrieves relevant documents and generates natural language answers.

query.description: The query text to search for in the knowledge base.

mode.description: Query mode: local (entity-focused), global (relationship patterns), hybrid (combined), naive (vector search), mix (knowledge graph + vector), bypass (direct LLM).

only_need_context.description: If true, only returns the retrieved context without generating a response.

only_need_prompt.description: If true, only returns the generated prompt without producing a response.

response_type.description: Defines the response format. Examples: 'Multiple Paragraphs', 'Single Paragraph', 'Bullet Points'.

top_k.description: Number of top items to retrieve. Represents entities in 'local' mode and relationships in 'global' mode.

chunk_top_k.description: Number of text chunks to retrieve from vector search.

max_total_tokens.description: Maximum total tokens budget for query context.

hl_keywords.description: High-level keywords to prioritize in retrieval.

ll_keywords.description: Low-level keywords to refine retrieval focus.

conversation_history.description: Past conversation history for context. Format: [{'role': 'user/assistant', 'content': 'message'}].

user_prompt.description: Custom user prompt to guide LLM response generation (does not affect retrieval).

enable_rerank.description: Enable reranking for retrieved text chunks.

include_references.description: If true, includes reference list in responses.

include_chunk_content.description: If true, includes actual chunk text content in references.

workspace.description: Optional LightRAG workspace (tenant) to query. Use the same name the documents were ingested under (e.g. 'customer_service', 'product_details'). Omit to query the server's default workspace.

tools.name: wait_for_rag_completion
tools.description: Wait for RAG ingestion to complete by polling track_id status. Blocks until all documents are processed/failed or timeout. Use this when you need to query the documents immediately after ingestion. Timeout is auto-calculated: (file_size_kb / 10) * 60 + 180 seconds.

track_id.description: The track_id returned from ragify or ragify_async tool.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often to check status (default: 15 seconds).

timeout_seconds.description: Max time to wait in seconds. If not provided, defaults to 600 seconds (10 minutes).

max_retries.description: Max consecutive poll failures before giving up (default: 3).

workspace.description: Optional LightRAG workspace (tenant). Must match the workspace that was used when the track_id was created by ragify / ragify_async.

tools.name: ragify_async
tools.description: Ingest documents into LightRAG with optional async completion notification. Fire-and-forget by default. Set on_complete=true to receive a notification in the task queue when processing finishes. Timeout is auto-calculated from file size: (size_kb / 10) * 60 + 180 seconds.

file_paths.description: List of file paths to upload and index.

text.description: Direct text content to insert (alternative to file_paths).

file_source.description: Optional source identifier for the inserted text.

on_complete.description: If true, monitor completion and send notification to task queue when done.

notify_task_id.description: Target task ID for completion notification. If task ends, falls back to chat task.

notify_chat_id.description: Fallback chat ID for notification if original task is ended.

timeout_seconds.description: Max time to monitor for completion. Auto-calculated from file size if not provided.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often to check status when monitoring (default: 15 seconds).

notification_message.description: Custom message to include in the completion notification.

workspace.description: Optional LightRAG workspace (tenant) name for data isolation. Use the same name consistently per category. The background completion monitor will poll track status scoped to this workspace.

tools.name: rag_replace_document
tools.description: Re-ingest a file into LightRAG after it has been edited on disk. Deletes any existing copies in the workspace whose filename matches (by basename), then uploads the new version. Use this — NOT plain ragify — when a source file's contents have changed; otherwise the knowledge graph keeps stale entries from the previous version. Re-ingest is asynchronous on the server side: the tool returns as soon as the upload is queued. Pair with wait_for_rag_completion if you need the new contents query-ready before continuing.

path.description: Absolute local path to the NEW version of the file to ingest.

workspace.description: Optional LightRAG workspace (tenant). Both the lookup of old copies and the re-ingest are scoped to this workspace. LEAVE EMPTY for the server's default workspace.

match_basename.description: When true (default), match old copies by filename only — handy when the new file lives in a different folder than the original ingest path. Set false to require an exact file_path string match instead.

tools.name: query_sales_db
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL query against the structured sales / inventory database. Use this INSTEAD of rag_query whenever the user asks for exact numbers, IDs, prices, stock levels, order status, shipment tracking, customer records, or any data where paraphrasing would be wrong. Only SELECT / WITH queries are accepted; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL are blocked. The tool returns columns + rows as structured metadata plus a Markdown-table preview as text.

sql.description: A single SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) statement. Use parameter placeholders ('?') for any user-provided values and pass them via `params`. Example: 'SELECT order_id, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC'.

params.description: Positional bind parameters for '?' placeholders in the SQL. Strongly preferred over string-interpolating user input into the query.

row_limit.description: Max rows to return (default 200, hard cap 5000).

db_path.description: Optional override for the SQLite database file path. Normally leave empty and let the server use the ECAN_SALES_DB_PATH environment variable.

tools.name: query_price

Use this — NOT rag_query — whenever the customer asks 'how much', '多少钱', 'price', 'discount', 'sale price'. Returns structured JSON: {sku, found, price, currency, original_price?, promo?, ...}.

sku.description: Product SKU / item ID to price.

customer_id.description: Optional customer ID — lets the integration apply tier-specific or coupon prices.

vendor_id.description: Optional vendor / integration identifier (e.g. 'shopify', 'woocommerce', 'erp_v2'). Leave empty to use the deployment default from the ECAN_CUSTOMER_DATA_VENDOR env var.

tools.name: query_inventories
tools.description: <category>Customer Service</category><sub-category>Lookup</sub-category>Look up real-time inventory / stock-on-hand for a SKU by delegating to the customer's commerce platform integration. Use this — NOT rag_query — whenever the customer asks 'in stock', '有货吗', '现货', 'available', 'restock'. Returns structured JSON: {sku, found, on_hand, reserved?, warehouses?, ...}.

warehouse_id.description: Optional warehouse / location filter. Leave empty for an aggregated total across all warehouses.

vendor_id.description: Optional vendor / integration identifier (e.g. 'shopify', 'woocommerce', 'erp_v2'). Leave empty to use the deployment default from the ECAN_CUSTOMER_DATA_VENDOR env var.

tools.name: query_order
tools.description: <category>Customer Service</category><sub-category>Lookup</sub-category>Look up an order by its ID and return status / shipping / tracking metadata by delegating to the customer's commerce platform integration. Use this — NOT rag_query — whenever the customer asks about 'my order', '订单', 'tracking number', 'shipping status', 'delivery date', 'refund status'. Returns structured JSON: {order_id, found, status, total, items, tracking_number?, carrier?, eta?, ...}.

order_id.description: Order ID provided by the customer.

customer_id.description: Optional customer ID — some integrations require it to authorize the lookup.

vendor_id.description: Optional vendor / integration identifier (e.g. 'shopify', 'woocommerce', 'erp_v2'). Leave empty to use the deployment default from the ECAN_CUSTOMER_DATA_VENDOR env var.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description: <category>Customer Service</category><sub-category>Shipping</sub-category>Check current weather for one or more places to set realistic delivery expectations. Call this when a customer asks about shipping / delivery time ('多久能到', '什么时候发货', 'when will it arrive') AND you know the ship-from location (from the product / warehouse). Include the customer's destination ONLY if they volunteered it — do not guess a destination. If severe weather (storm / typhoon / heavy snow / heavy rain, 暴雨 / 台风 / 暴雪 …) hits the ship-from or destination, the result has severe=true and suggested_delay_days so you can tell the customer delivery may take a few extra days. Returns JSON: {vendor, results:[{location, condition, severe, severity, delay_days}], severe, suggested_delay_days, advisory}.

tools.name: query_qa_history

Returns JSON: {status, count, rows:[{id, store_id, product_id, platform, question, answer, created_at}]}.

owner.description: Optional: only this account owner's turns.

tools.name: propose_kb_candidate
tools.description: <category>Knowledge Base</category><sub-category>Mining</sub-category>Propose ONE new Q&A entry for the knowledge base, for the merchant to approve. Call this after clustering the captured history, for each distinct question the KB does not already answer well. The candidate is saved as 'pending' and the merchant is notified; it does NOT enter the KB until they approve. Pass source_ids (the qa_history row ids the candidate was mined from) so those turns are not re-processed. Returns {candidate_id, ok}.

answer.description: The proposed answer to add to the KB.

rationale.description: Why this is worth adding / what gap it fills.

store_id.description: Store this Q&A pertains to, if store-specific.

product_id.description: 商品ID this Q&A pertains to, if product-specific.

source_ids.description: qa_history row ids this candidate was mined from.

tools.name: add_timer

period_ms.description: Interval between fires in milliseconds (e.g. 15000 for 15 seconds, 60000 for 1 minute).

tools.name: subscribe_browser_event

domain.description: CDP domain to subscribe to. Common domains: 'Network' (requests/responses), 'Page' (navigation/lifecycle), 'DOM' (mutations), 'Runtime' (console/exceptions), 'Console' (console messages).

event_method.description: Full CDP event method in 'Domain.eventName' format. Examples: 'Network.responseReceived', 'Page.frameNavigated', 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled', 'DOM.attributeModified', 'Page.javascriptDialogOpening'.

label.description: User-friendly label for this subscription, used as routing key (e.g. 'price_api', 'page_loaded', 'dom_change'). Must be unique per agent.

filter_expr.description: Optional filter expression. Syntax: '<field> <op> <value>' where op is contains/==/!=//startswith/endswith. Nested fields use dots. Examples: "response.url contains 'api/price'", "response.status == 200", "type == XHR". If omitted, all events of this method will match.

tools.name: unsubscribe_browser_event

label.description: The label of the subscription to remove. Either sub_id or label must be provided.

tools.name: consult_skill_editor

Call this FIRST and immediately for those topics — do NOT clarify locally or ask the user for files / paths / formats first. The cloud Skill Editor agent has full access to the user's skills, flowgrams, skill-editor tools (canvas ops, validation, plan generation, log ingest), and will either answer, ask a clarifying question, return an implementation plan, or generate a flowgram diff. Pass the user's question verbatim plus any context they provided (skill name, log snippet, error text). DO NOT use this for ordinary chitchat or questions you can clearly answer with the other available tools yourself.

prompt.description: The user's question, restated clearly. Include any context the user has provided (skill name, log snippet, error message).

tools.name: hand_off_to_skill_editor
tools.description: TRANSFER the conversation to the cloud Skills page so the user can continue with the full Skill Editor UX (canvas, clarification cards, plan review, flowgram apply, validation). Call this — INSTEAD of consult_skill_editor — whenever the user wants a MULTI-TURN workflow: creating a new skill, modifying an existing skill, or doing in-depth log analysis. Examples that should trigger handoff: 'create a new skill that …', 'modify the order-sync skill', 'help me debug why this skill stalls', 'analyze this log file and find the root cause'. Use consult_skill_editor instead for one-shot questions you can answer in a single bubble ('what does pend_event do?'). Pass the user's question verbatim; the Skills page will open and seed its chat input with the message so the user can hit Send (or edit first).

user_message.description: The user's request, verbatim or lightly cleaned up. This is what gets seeded into the Skills-page chat.

auto_send.description: If true, the Skills page will auto-send the seeded message on arrival. If false (default), the message is only prefilled into the input box so the user can review/edit before clicking Send.
